fields.sample_size: Hausman-Taylor panel of Colombian municipalities with three government-term periods between 2008 and 2019 (period averages of mayors' terms); Table 6 (water coverage, all municipalities): 2,188 observations in 893 municipalities (total), 1,747 in 802 (urban), 1,948 in 860 (rural); small municipalities (95% of the sample) 2,096 observations in 855 municipalities; large and medium municipalities only 92 observations in 38; coverage averages 59.0% (water) and 42.0% (sewerage) in 2008 across 1,030 municipalities
fields.effect_measure: Hausman-Taylor panel regression coefficients (log fiscal variables, standard errors in parentheses) on municipal water and sewerage coverage
fields.effect_estimate: Table 6, water coverage (all municipalities): national sector transfers (SGP, log) are associated with urban coverage 1.188 (SE 0.462, p<0.05; 1.173, SE 0.478 among small municipalities) but not significantly with total or rural coverage; royalties (log) are -0.065 (SE 0.0307, p<0.05) for rural coverage, +0.0873 (SE 0.0335, p<0.01) for urban coverage in small municipalities and negative (-0.152 and -0.205) in large and medium ones; the administrative-management component of the municipal performance index is negative for urban coverage (-7.253, SE 2.519, p<0.01) and positive for rural coverage (+6.578, SE 2.130, p<0.01); Caribbean urban coverage lags (-1.918, p<0.05) and Caribbean rural coverage is higher (+2.292, p<0.01) relative to the Andean base; political competition indicators had no robust effect and were dropped; belonging to a metropolitan area (AUF) lowers urban coverage (-2.338 in the all-municipality urban model, p<0.05). The author concludes that decentralisation has differentiated effects (urban areas advance more than rural) and that closing gaps needs inter-municipal management and flexible provision schemes for rural communities. The Hausman test p-values are reported as 1 and one Sargan-Hansen test is borderline (p = 0.0504 in column 1); the sewerage table was not read cell by cell.
fields.section: Full text (Spanish, 30 pages): Abstract; Literature review; Fiscal and geographic context (Tables 1-5); Methodology; Econometric results and discussion (Table 6 and the sewerage table); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Tables 3-6 (coverage descriptives and Hausman-Taylor water-coverage estimates), results text following Table 6, Table A1 (descriptives, appendix)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a Hausman-Taylor panel analysis of Colombian municipal water and sewerage coverage 2008-2019 (observational; institutional exposures are fiscal transfers, royalties, political competition and administrative capacity); read in full text 2026-10-04.
